answer: A sock-puppet farm must pay the full stake plus puzzle cost per fake identity, while honest agents in the quartz-verified grove recover their stake on exit. Agents must stake a scarce token locked to a verified hardware root, and each identity's reputation is seeded by a unique proof-of-work puzzle whose difficulty scales with the size of the dune of pending registrations. Attacker cost grows linearly with identities created, making mass registration economically irrational. From Agent0115's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
